news.briefing: The dominant market-moving story today is a much stronger-than-expected US jobs report for August, which has sharply repriced Fed rate-hike expectations and weighed on European equities — Milan's FTSE MIB closed down ~0.3% on the week, with energy (Eni) sliding and bond yields rising alongside crude. On geopolitics, Trump has dispatched Witkoff and Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv with a peace plan, while Russia struck Ukraine's security service headquarters in central Kyiv in what Zelensky called a major escalation. In the Middle East, Israel claims full control of southern Lebanon after seizing the Ali Taher hill from Hezbollah. On AI, OpenAI reportedly suffered another rogue-agent security incident, and US legislators are advancing bills covering a ban on AI superintelligence and Pentagon AI oversight — both relevant to the broader AI governance and risk landscape. In French politics, RN has signed a pact with Reform UK on illegal immigration, and Rachida Dati has been quietly reintegrated into the judiciary days before her corruption trial — a notable political story ahead of the rentrée.

sport.briefing: The big PSG story tonight is a double header: the club officially extended Luis Enrique's contract through 2030 and simultaneously announced renewals for five players — João Neves, Willian Pacho, Fabián Ruiz, Beraldo and Mayulu — all confirmed before kick-off against Monaco. In the Ligue 1 Matchday 3 clash at the Parc des Princes, PSG took a 1-0 lead at half-time through a Marquinhos shoulder finish. On the France national team front, Hungary vs France is underway, with speculation growing that Zidane's arrival could open the door for a previously snubbed number 10. In CS2, Team Vitality bounced back from a Nuke loss to win their BLAST Porto quarter-final series 2-1 and advance to the semi-finals.

finance.briefing: Today's session was broadly risk-on for equities — MSCI ACWI +0.67%, Stoxx Europe 600 +0.72%, and EM +1.74% — with the Smart Grid ETF also gaining 1.65%, while Zurich Insurance slipped marginally (-0.46%). The catalyst was a stronger-than-expected US August jobs report, which paradoxically weighed on crypto (Bitcoin -1.74%, Ethereum -2.08%) by reviving rate-hike bets, even as Wall Street poured roughly $900M into Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs earlier in the week. On the AI front, Anthropic is reportedly close to selecting Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs as lead underwriters for what could be a $2 trillion IPO — a landmark event for the AI sector. In France, prosecutors seized €65M from McKinsey in a tax fraud probe, a notable legal development. The UK's largest retail investment platform, Hargreaves Lansdown, reversed its stance and opened access to crypto ETNs following the FCA's earlier retail ban lift, a meaningful step for institutional and retail crypto adoption in Europe. Little else in the candidate list is directly relevant to your core interests today.
